topicName: Locking Mechanisms: Record, Gap, and Next-Key Locks
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Understanding MySQL Locking Mechanisms: Record, Gap, and Next-Key Locks"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Concurrency control is critical for maintaining data integrity in relational databases. In MySQL, the InnoDB storage engine handles concurrency using sophisticated locking strategies. While basic locks like shared and exclusive locks are common knowledge, mastering Record, Gap, and Next-Key locks is essential for understanding how InnoDB prevents race conditions, non-repeatable reads, and phantom reads."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"The Baseline: Transaction Isolation Levels"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before diving into lock types, it is important to note that Gap and Next-Key locks are primarily used when operating under the REPEATABLE READ isolation level. This isolation level is the default in MySQL InnoDB and requires special locking behavior to satisfy ACID compliance, particularly regarding phantom reads."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Record Locks"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"A Record Lock is the most granular lock type in InnoDB. It locks an index record directly. Even if a table has no explicitly defined primary key or unique indexes, InnoDB creates a hidden clustered index and applies record locks to that index structure."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = 10 FOR UPDATE;"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"In the example above, a Record Lock is placed specifically on the index record where id equals 10. No other transaction can modify or delete that exact row until the current transaction commits or rolls back."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Gap Locks"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"A Gap Lock is a lock on a gap between index records, or a lock on the gap before the first or after the last index record. Gap locks are purely inhibitory; their sole purpose is to prevent other transactions from inserting new rows into the gap. This prevents phantom reads."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id BETWEEN 10 AND 20 FOR UPDATE;"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"If rows with ids 10 and 20 exist, a gap lock will lock the space between 10 and 20. Even if no row exists with id 15, another transaction attempting to insert id 15 will be forced to wait until the gap lock is released."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Next-Key Locks"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"A Next-Key Lock is a combination of a Record Lock on the index record and a Gap Lock on the gap before the index record. This is the default locking mechanism used by InnoDB in REPEATABLE READ mode for range scans."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"It locks the specific index record."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"It locks the gap immediately preceding that index record."},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"By using next-key locks, InnoDB prevents other transactions from both modifying existing rows within the range and inserting new rows into the gaps covered by the scan."},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Practical Demonstration"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Consider a table named 'inventory' with an indexed column 'quantity' containing values 10, 20, and 30. If you execute a query searching for values greater than 15, InnoDB places next-key locks on the index records and their preceding gaps."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"SELECT * FROM inventory WHERE quantity >= 20 FOR UPDATE;"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"This lock setup covers the record 20, the gap between 10 and 20, the record 30, the gap between 20 and 30, and the supremum record (the imaginary record that represents positive infinity). Consequently, inserting a quantity of 25 is blocked."},{"order":22,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary and Best Practices"},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Record Locks lock individual index rows."},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Gap Locks prevent insertions into spaces between index records to avoid phantom reads."},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Next-Key Locks combine both to secure ranges during REPEATABLE READ operations."},{"order":26,"type":"paragraph","text":"To minimize lock contention and avoid deadlocks, ensure your queries utilize proper indexes. Unindexed queries cause InnoDB to fall back to locking entire tables or larger gaps than necessary, severely degrading concurrent performance."}]
